entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Wenceslaus II Přemyslid was King of Bohemia (1278–1305), Duke of Cracow (1291–1305), and King of Poland (1296–1305). He succeeded his brother Wenceslaus I as King of Bohemia and expanded the kingdom's borders through strategic alliances and military campaigns. Wenceslaus II's reign saw the establishment of trade routes and the growth of cities, laying the groundwork for Bohemia's future prosperity. His legacy as a just and fair ruler helped to foster a sense of national identity among the Bohemian people. The chronicler Matthew of Parma praised Wenceslaus II as a 'great king, whose goodness and justice were renowned throughout Christendom.' Despite his military successes, Wenceslaus II's reign was cut short by his untimely death on June 29, 1305, at the age of approximately 30. His successor, Wenceslaus III, struggled to live up to his brother's example, leading to a period of instability and conflict in Bohemia.

His legacy as a just and fair ruler helped to foster a sense of national identity among the Bohemian people.
